attribution_limitations: The echocardiogram images in Figure 3 print overlay ejection fractions (Teich method) that differ from the ejection fractions the case text gives for the same studies (presentation, 6 h before the second arrest, and just after extracorporeal CPR). The text does not name its measurement method.

The Supplementary Figure 1 legend (the article's own supplementary-material caption in the source XML, not a text segment and not content of the supplement file) says the EKG with newly developed T wave inversion on V1-V3 was on hospital day 3, while the case text places the T wave inversion on the next day (hospital day four) after the day-3 arrest. Two different hospital days for one finding: source conflict on the time attribute only.

The text says both ventricular walls were markedly thickened up to about 13 mm just after ECMO pump on, while the Figure 3 caption gives 13.6 mm for the LV posterior wall and 11.8 mm for the septum, with the right ventricle wall thickened, for the same study. The approximate text value and the caption values are an approximation difference, not two values for one wall.

The text says the endomyocardial biopsy was positive for T-lymphocytic infiltration, and the discussion says O. tsutsugamushi PCR and immunohistochemical stain on biopsy tissue "failed"; whether this means a technical failure or a negative result is not stated.
Meningoencephalitis is hedged in the case description ("suggesting") but listed among the patient's complications in the discussion.

The case text calls the referring facility a private hospital, while the discussion calls it a private clinic and says a proper antibiotic was initiated 10 days from symptom onset; treatment given at the referring facility is not described.

The antibody was reported converted positive on hospital day 19 yet the patient is said to have been discharged about 10 days after transfer to the ward; the discharge day and whether the antibody result preceded discharge are not stated.

Supplementary Table 1 versus the case text: (1) troponin T 0.231 ng/ml carries reference value < 0.005 ng/ml in the text but 0-0.014 in the table (labelled high sensitivity Troponin-T); (2) the white blood cell count 9,800 has unit /ul in the text but /mL in the table. Supplement-vs-article contradictions: the text facts here and SM2 rows f01 and f25 are review_only source conflicts.
Figure 2 (an image-only course summary) prints labels such as a Pseudomonas aeruginosa bloodstream infection that the article text does not state; these are pixel content only.
